description: Job Title: Business Analyst Job Description The Business Analyst plays a key role in translating business, user, and product needs into clear, actionable requirements that support software and platform development in a complex, compliance-driven environment. This position partners closely with product, engineering, and quality assurance teams to ensure requirements are technically sound, testable, and fully traceable across the system lifecycle. Responsibilities Elicit, analyze, and document business, user, and product requirements that capture functional, non-functional, and compliance-related needs. Job Title: Construction Analyst Job Description The Construction Analyst provides advanced analytical support to the construction team for complex projects. This role focuses on data collection, reporting, and performance tracking, while taking a lead role in the preparation and management of project budgets, including detailed cost estimation, tracking, and variance analysis. The Construction Analyst independently gathers, organizes, and analyzes data related to project progress, expenses, and resource allocation, and collaborates closely with cross-functional teams to produce insightful construction reports and presentations. The position is highly visible within project operations and contributes directly to strategic decision-making, continuous improvement, and innovation in construction analytics. Responsibilities Provide advanced analytical support to the construction team for complex utility and infrastructure projects. Lead the preparation and management of project budgets, including detailed cost estimation, ongoing cost tracking, and in-depth variance analysis. Independently collect, organize, and analyze data related to project progress, expenses, materials planning, and resource allocation, ensuring accuracy and completeness. Develop and maintain project tracking mechanisms to monitor key milestones, work orders, and overall project performance. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather, synthesize, and analyze data for construction reports and executive-level presentations. Generate comprehensive reports, visualizations, and dashboards that clearly communicate project status, KPIs, and critical metrics to stakeholders. Support construction management and administration activities, including contracts administration and construction documentation. Assist with invoice reconciliation and financial reporting to ensure alignment between project costs, budgets, and contractual obligations. Coordinate project meetings, including scheduling, documenting discussions, capturing action items, and tracking follow-up tasks. Evaluate vendor and contractor performance using data-driven criteria and provide strategic input for supplier management and procurement decisions. Contribute to supplier relationship management by providing performance insights and recommendations based on analytical findings. Apply construction analytics expertise to environments with several moving parts and diverse stakeholders, including power distribution, substation, and utility construction projects. Leverage tools and systems such as CAMP, JETS, and other project or asset management platforms to support tracking and reporting activities. Stay current with industry trends, best practices, and emerging technologies in construction analytics and apply them to drive continuous improvement. Job Title: Laboratory Analyst Job Description The Laboratory Analyst supports a busy analytical laboratory in Liverpool, NY by preparing, analyzing, and generating final reports for solid samples using Glow Discharge Mass Spectrometry (GDMS). The role focuses on a wide range of materials, including metals, powders, ceramics, and coatings, and requires careful sample preparation, operation of analytical instrumentation, and troubleshooting of processes and equipment. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to high-quality analytical work within a structured, standards-driven environment. Responsibilities Prepare solid samples for analysis, including metals, powders, ceramics, and coatings, using bench top shears, hand-held metal snips, precision saws, polishers, grinding wheels, and various acids. Perform analyses of prepared samples using Glow Discharge Mass Spectrometry (GDMS) in accordance with established laboratory procedures and quality standards. Generate accurate and timely final reports based on analytical results, ensuring data integrity and clear documentation. Troubleshoot laboratory processes and equipment to identify root causes of issues and implement effective corrective actions. Use microscopes, ICP-OES, ICP-MS, gas analyzers, and associated instrumentation as part of testing and analytical workflows. Plan and prioritize daily tasks and responsibilities to meet project deadlines and customer requirements. Perform analyses and design experiments with some supervision, following scientific best practices and laboratory protocols. Build and maintain strong internal and external customer relationships, delivering solutions tailored to customer needs. Actively contribute to a positive team environment by valuing collaboration, empathy, consensus, and mutual respect. Comply with ISO standards and company information security requirements in all aspects of laboratory work and data handling. Demonstrate a proactive approach to self-development by seeking growth and challenges through diverse learning opportunities. Adhere to all laboratory safety procedures, including proper handling of acids, tools, and equipment used in sample preparation. Support continuous improvement of laboratory methods, processes, and documentation where appropriate. Essential Skills Bachelor’s degree in materials science, chemistry, or a related field. At least 2 years of relevant laboratory experience. Hands-on experience with testing and associated instrumentation such as microscopes, ICP-OES, ICP-MS, and gas analyzers. Ability to plan and prioritize tasks and responsibilities in a dynamic laboratory environment. Demonstrated ability to perform analyses and design experiments with some supervision. Job Title: QC Analyst II Job Description The QC Analyst II plays a key role in ensuring the quality and compliance of raw materials, in-process samples, stability samples, and finished products within a GMP-regulated environment. This position performs routine and complex analytical testing, supports method development and optimization, and maintains rigorous documentation to meet regulatory and quality standards. The role actively promotes safe laboratory practices and contributes to continuous improvement across quality control operations. Responsibilities Demonstrate a strong commitment to laboratory safety, quality systems, and regulatory compliance in all daily operations. Support and promote a culture of safe laboratory practices by strictly following established environmental, health, and safety procedures. Perform routine analytical and laboratory testing on raw materials, in-process samples, stability samples, and finished products. Execute testing activities in accordance with approved analytical methods, internal quality standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Operate and maintain analytical instruments such as HPLC, Karl Fischer, UV/VIS spectrophotometers, and LCMS systems in a GMP environment. Review and verify analytical data for accuracy, completeness, and adherence to established specifications and acceptance criteria. Document experimental results clearly and accurately in laboratory records and electronic systems, ensuring data integrity and traceability. Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, summaries, and stability assessments based on analytical data and observations. Assist in the development, qualification, and optimization of analytical methods, protocols, and laboratory procedures. Support the creation, revision, and maintenance of controlled documentation, including standard operating procedures, test methods, and product specifications. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to investigate laboratory issues, support troubleshooting activities, and implement corrective and preventive actions. Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance laboratory efficiency, data quality, and compliance with cGMP requirements. Provide technical guidance, training, and mentorship to laboratory personnel as needed to ensure consistent application of methods and procedures. Essential Skills Bachelor’s degree (BS) in chemistry, biology, or a related scientific discipline. 2–5 years of experience as a QC analyst or chemist in a GMP or cGMP environment. Hands-on experience with analytical testing equipment and methodologies, including High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC). Practical experience with LCMS (Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry) techniques and instrumentation. Proficiency in Karl Fischer titration for moisture or water content determination. Experience with UV/VIS spectrophotometry and related analytical methods. Strong understanding of quality control principles and practices

Job Title: Mass Production Parts Quality Analyst Job Description This role focuses on ensuring the quality of mass production parts supplied to an OEM automotive assembly plant, with dedicated positions supporting weld suppliers and plastics suppliers. You will lead detailed analysis of quality issues, collaborate closely with suppliers and internal manufacturing departments, and drive robust corrective and preventive actions using established quality tools and systems. Responsibilities Lead in-depth analysis of quality problems, including detailed parts measurements, to identify root causes and implement actions that minimize impact on downstream manufacturing departments. Prepare and submit clear, technical documentation of quality issues to suppliers using the NARS Honda Trouble Report (HTR) system, ensuring issues are communicated effectively and countermeasure activities are initiated promptly. Set and define technical requirements for supplier part change points using the NA Change Point Control System (CPCS), and thoroughly evaluate supplier quality documents before management approval. Conduct complex problem-solving analyses and investigations to resolve recurring or high-impact quality concerns affecting weld or plastic components. Lead supplier Quality Assurance Visits (QAVs) to communicate concerns, verify implementation of countermeasures, and confirm that non-conforming conditions have been eliminated. Mentor new associates within the group on problem-solving methods, quality procedures, and the responsibilities of the Parts Quality function. Perform judgment, disposition, and handling activities for non-conforming parts, including deciding on rework, repair, or rejection as appropriate. Evaluate and judge the quality of parts received from suppliers to ensure they meet established specifications and standards. Effectively solve quality problems using PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) and structured root cause analysis techniques. Review and approve supplier countermeasures and supplier change points before they are released for production use. Essential Skills Bachelor’s degree in Engineering. At least 2 years of quality engineering experience, preferably in an automotive manufacturing environment. Hands-on experience with quality engineering practices, including root cause and corrective action (RCCA). Strong expereince in quality assurance within mass production or automotive manufacturing. Working knowledge of TS16949 or similar automotive quality management standards. Experience using core quality tools such as Fishbone diagrams, 8D, 5WHY, and RCCA. Ability to apply PFMEA (Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) in evaluating and mitigating process risks. Proficiency in structured problem-solving methods, including PDCA. Strong analytical skills to interpret measurement data and assess part conformance. Effective written and verbal communication skills to prepare technical reports and interact with suppliers and internal stakeholders
